rule: a manifest naming a chunk the build did not emit
why:
AND THE OTHER END OF THE SAME GATE: a manifest naming a chunk the build did not emit. Every byte `bundle` reports is read by name out of that manifest, and the read had nothing between it and the disk, so the gate died with a Node stack trace and `run.mjs` reported it red with no sentence in it. The fixture names one chunk and does not put it there, and one finding is what proves the gate names the file rather than counting the manifest.

ITS TREE IS SHAPED BY A GUARD UPSTREAM OF THE ONE UNDER TEST, which is about mtimes rather than contents and is the only reason this fixture looks odd. The shell lives under `apps/site/src/` and there is no `apps/web/src/` at all, because a checkout writes `.svelte-kit/` before `src/` and a source file newer than the manifest makes the gate skip as stale before it reads a chunk.

AND THERE IS NO `packages/` HERE, WHICH IS A SECOND THING THIS FIXTURE NOW PROVES. It used to carry a `packages/seeded/` holding nothing but a manifest, because the staleness walk read `packages/` with a bare `readdir` and died on a tree without one. `85c44aa7` gave that walk the `.catch` its sibling over `apps/` has always had, so the decoy came out: if the guard is ever removed again, this fixture goes red with an ENOENT stack where its sentence should be. One violation is still seeded and one finding is still asserted; the absent directory is a property of the tree rather than a second violation.
